note: WIDE funnel for the single 'science' category, restricted to its allowed_domains. Science window = 14 days / 336h (start ~2026-07-18T22:00Z). Every item's published date was extracted from og article:published_time / JSON-LD / byline via WebFetch and gated FRESH with `python3 pipeline/freshness.py <iso> 2026-08-01T22:00:36Z science`. Aligned to TODAY's rotation (astronomy/ML cosmology, quantum ML, research/lab automation, AI cognition/neuroscience) and steered clear of yesterday's saturated beats (quantum-chemistry OLED, ocean-current/GOFLOW climate ML, material-rules ML, protein/enzyme, genomics, QEC, drug discovery, batteries). Outlet diversity: phys.org (3, at the =3 collection cap), thequantuminsider.com (1), sciencedaily.com (1) = 3 distinct outlets; ax-curator tightens to <=2/outlet downstream. WHY not wider: WebSearch budget (200 calls) was exhausted mid-run by the parallel librarians, and newscientist.com is blocked to our agent. DROPPED as STALE after date-check: statnews 'teens turn to chatbots' (Jul 2), eurekalert McBain adolescent-chatbot release (Jun 1) and 'chatbots worsen mental illness' (Feb 23), sciencedaily heart-blood-test CardiOmicScore (Jul 16, 16d) and neutron-star merger sims (Jun 26), superconductor ML (Jul 1). DROPPED unverifiable (no extractable published date, never guessed): space.com 'ExoMiner++ 10,091 exoplanets'. DROPPED per relevance rule: MIT Tech Review AI-drug-design/superintelligence/AI-hiring-bias (drug-discovery on avoid + AI-industry noise). No social channels defined for science -> none collected.

items.title: First AI-driven telescope goes stargazing
items.excerpt: Scientists from Northwestern, University of Chicago and Fermilab deployed a reinforcement-learning AI to autonomously schedule Dark Energy Camera observations, adapting the plan in real time as sky and weather conditions change -- a milestone toward self-running observatories, with performance the team rates comparable to a human scheduler.

items.title: AI agent helps prepare synchrotron X-ray experimental measurements, paving the way for autonomous operation
items.excerpt: Stanford and SLAC researchers built an AI agent that autonomously aligns crystal samples at synchrotron X-ray beamlines -- reading detector images, experiment logs and scan results, then issuing instrument-control commands -- a step toward self-driving experimental facilities that free scientists from routine setup.

items.title: AI 'brain age' from sleep EEG flags sharply higher dementia risk
items.excerpt: UCSF researchers used machine learning on overnight sleep-EEG recordings from about 7,000 adults to estimate each person's 'brain age'; brains scoring older than the person's actual age were tied to a sharply elevated risk of developing dementia -- an AI biomarker turning routine sleep data into early neurological insight.
